title: Topographic and Orthophoto Maps
summary: Features of topographic and orthophoto maps, reading the map reference and grid, identifying landforms from contour patterns, and using the two maps together.

notes.text: A **topographic map** shows natural and human-made features of an area using symbols, colours and contour lines. In South Africa, the standard scale is **1 : 50 000**. Each map sheet has a reference number based on latitude and longitude, e.g. **2628CB JOHANNESBURG**: 26° S, 28° E, block C, sub-block B.

An **orthophoto map** is an aerial photograph taken vertically from an aircraft, corrected so that distances are accurate, with **contour lines** (brown or orange), names and some symbols added. The standard scale is **1 : 10 000**, so it is a larger scale than a topographic map and shows more detail of a smaller area.

rows: Routes, relief, settlement patterns across a region
Individual buildings, fields, land-use and erosion

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: On an orthophoto, identify features by **tone** (dark or light), **texture** (smooth or rough) and **shape**. Water is usually dark and smooth; cultivated fields appear as regular patterns; trees look rough and dark; roads are thin light lines.

rows: Closed, roughly circular contours with the highest in the centre
Flat top with steep sides: contours close together around the edge, a wide space in the middle
Like a mesa, but much smaller in area at the top
V-shaped contours pointing UPHILL (towards higher ground); usually a river in the valley
V-shaped contours pointing DOWNHILL (towards lower ground)
A low area between two hills
Contours very close together or merging, in a long line

notes.text: Position on a topographic map is given in **degrees, minutes and seconds** of latitude and longitude, read from the edges of the map, e.g. **26°12′30″ S, 28°02′45″ E**. Each minute has 60 seconds. The latitude is always given first.

A **cross-section** shows the shape of the land along a line between two points, as if the land were cut through. It is drawn from the heights where the line crosses each contour. It can show whether two points are **intervisible** (whether you could see one from the other): if higher ground lies between them, they are not intervisible.

✓ Dark tone and smooth texture (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how a cross-section shows whether two points are intervisible.
questions.memo:
✓ It shows the height of the land between the two points (1)
✓ If higher ground lies in between, it blocks the view, so they are not intervisible (1)
